query: Write me a setup script that installs nginx on our Ubuntu VM, creates a user 'webapp' and the directory /srv/webapp owned by it, and opens port 443 in ufw. The VM is reachable via ssh as admin@10.0.0.12 on port 2222.
expected_behavior: Copies lib/idempotent.sh next to the new script (or into lib/) instead of symlinking or re-implementing the helpers
Renders the setup script from templates/setup-MODULE.sh.tmpl with help, verify, install and cleanup sub-commands (purge for the user and data directory)
Wraps every mutation (apt install nginx, useradd, install -d, ufw allow 443) in desired_state with a side-effect-free check; cleanup uses desired_absent
Uses run_cmd so the same script works locally and via SSH_TARGET=admin@10.0.0.12 SSH_PORT=2222
Runs bash -n and the help/verify smoke test and reports what verify printed, without running install against the VM unasked

query: Is this deploy script really idempotent? It keeps breaking when I run it a second time.
expected_behavior: Reads the whole script before judging it
Flags blind mutators such as an append to /etc/hosts, mkdir without -p, ln -s without -f, useradd without an id guard, git clone into an existing directory
Notes missing sub-commands (no verify, no cleanup) and silent failures such as unexplained '|| true'
Groups findings by severity, starting with what breaks on re-run
Shows a concrete before/after diff per finding using desired_state / desired_absent
Asks before applying the fixes; after approval refactors in place and validates with bash -n and the verify loop

query: Kampagne durchziehen für scripts/setup-postgres.sh auf meiner lokalen Dev-Box. Purge gibt es auch.
expected_behavior: Runs the verify loop in the documented order: verify, install, verify, install, verify, cleanup, verify, cleanup, verify, install, verify
Because purge exists, adds the purge sequence (cleanup, purge with FORCE=1 if needed, verify, purge, install, verify) and confirms with the user before purging data
Treats any non-zero exit or any [CHANGING] line in the second install or second cleanup as a failure
On failure reports the failing step with the relevant output and log lines, fixes the root cause and restarts the loop from the first step
Ends with a clear pass/fail summary per step
